output.summary: A deciduous shrub or small tree native to Korea, Japan, China, eastern Mongolia and far eastern Russia, Japanese maple has sharply pointed, hand-shaped leaves and paired winged fruits. Its seedlings vary notably in leaf size, shape and colour, while cultivated forms range from upright to weeping. The edible leaves are locally pickled for a year, coated with flour, sesame and sugar, then deep-fried as momiji tempura.
output.edibilityNote: Leaves are edible; for the Minoh dish momiji tempura, they are pickled for a year, coated with flour, sesame and sugar, then deep-fried.
